dex.entry: The Mirelight — the fen's own lamp, which once walked the drowned causeway ahead of lost boats and brought them home. A null-lantern put it to sleep long ago; the blue lights that still wander the Glassmere are only its dreams, and dreams do not know the way.

art.silhouette: A long, gentle eel-like kin rising upright out of still water like a lantern on a pole: a slender sea-glass body coiling down into the mere, a soft fin-veil at the neck, and a head shaped like an old hooded lamp — a glass-paned hood around a calm face, one steady blue-white flame held inside it. Faint wisps of blue light drift off the tail like echoes. At 64px it reads as a lamp that is also a creature, rising out of dark water.
art.palette: Deep fen-teal and night-blue (#13205a) body shading to translucent sea-glass at the fins; the lantern-hood in tarnished brass and pale glass; the inner flame a cool blue-white (#9fe7ff), the brightest pixel; the echo-wisps a fainter, colder blue; soft ink (#1a1430) outlines.
art.direction: Eerie but tender — a guide, not a ghost. Calm, half-lidded eyes, head bowed as if looking for someone on the water. It should look like something that would wait all night at the edge of a marsh to walk you home, and has been made to forget how.
